title: The Complexity Paradox

naturalwine.insight: High comment/like ratio (4.68%) — content here drives debate and disagreement. Naturalwine is polarising in a way that maps directly to the complexity paradox thesis. Engaged, opinionated audience.

lowinterventionwine.insight: Smallest and most niche hashtag. High comment/like ratio (8%) suggests a tight, engaged community rather than broad reach. Producers and enthusiasts talking to each other — not a discovery channel.

winevalue.insight: Solid median engagement (225 likes) and good comment/like ratio. Value discussions attract genuine audience interest. Directly relevant to S2 (Price Was Never the Point).

wineeducation.insight: Highest average and median likes. Viral ceiling is enormous. Educational wine content has mainstream crossover appeal — the highest engagement numbers of all 7 hashtags confirm wine education is a high-interest content category on Instagram.

wset.insight: HIGHEST comment/like ratio of all 7 hashtags (10.44%). People studying WSET are intensely conversational — sharing experiences, asking questions, celebrating passes. The education community is the most interactive subset of wine social media despite lower raw reach.

orangewine.insight: High viral ceiling (32k likes), low median (134). Orange wine is a visual/aesthetic hashtag — people like and scroll but don't discuss much. Passive appreciation vs. active engagement.

everydaywine.insight: Second highest avg likes but extreme outlier skew (max 86k, median only 72). Everydaywine is the democratisation signal — a small number of posts break through to mass audiences, but most get modest engagement. The accessibility story in one dataset.

keyFindings.finding: Education drives the most engaged conversations
keyFindings.data: #wset has a 10.44% comment/like ratio — highest of all 7 hashtags. #wineeducation has the highest average likes (7,622) and median engagement (423). Wine learners are the most interactive community on Instagram.
keyFindings.relevance: S1 — The Palate Journey: the appetite for wine education is real and growing

keyFindings.finding: Natural wine is the most polarising hashtag
keyFindings.data: #naturalwine has a 4.68% comment/like ratio — second highest — with posts regularly driving hundreds of comments. The debate mirrors Reddit: quality vs. category, authenticity vs. intervention.
keyFindings.relevance: S1 — supports the complexity paradox framing: naturalwine discourse adds labels and noise, not clarity

keyFindings.finding: Value content punches above its weight
keyFindings.data: #winevalue has the strongest median/average balance of the mid-tier hashtags (median 225, avg 1,480, comment/like 2.81%). Value conversations are stable, not viral.
keyFindings.relevance: S2 — Price Was Never the Point: there is a genuine engaged audience for value/QPR content

keyFindings.finding: Everydaywine shows democratisation but not depth
keyFindings.data: #everydaywine median likes: 72. Max: 86,569. Extreme skew suggests accessibility of wine content but shallow engagement — people like and scroll, not discuss.
keyFindings.relevance: S2 — the accessibility paradox: wine is 'for everyone' but most everyday wine content doesn't generate serious conversation

keyFindings.finding: Low-intervention community is niche but committed
keyFindings.data: #lowinterventionwine: 39 posts, median 87 likes, 8% comment/like ratio. Small audience, highly engaged. A community of producers and serious enthusiasts.
keyFindings.relevance: S1 — niche expertise communities form around real taste preferences, not just marketing categories

notes: Posts scraped via scrapesmith/instagram-hashtag-scraper, 20 posts per hashtag (39–42 actual). Dataset includes full caption, timestamps, likes, comments, owner. Raw dataset ID: DCHLBYyEeZJm5ybdA. Instagram data cannot be relied on for 100% accuracy due to platform API limits.
